mainTopic: The משכן's curtains and wagons as the model for רשות הרבים, and how a pit and its bank combine to make a separate domain
overview: This amud finishes a description of the משכן's beauty: the clasps in the loops shone like stars. A ברייתא then teaches that the plain goat-hair curtains needed more חכמה than the fine lower curtains, because the women spun the hair while it was still on the goats. The גמרא returns to the משנה of the two balconies. רב, quoting רבי חייא, says the spaces under, between, and beside the wagons that carried the קרשים were רשות הרבים. אביי and רבא give the wagons' measurements and explain why the extra room was needed. The total comes to fifteen אמות, so the גמרא asks how a public road can be sixteen. It answers that one more אמה was where a לוי stood to catch slipping קרשים. A new משנה then teaches that a pit's bank or a rock that is ten טפחים high and four wide is its own domain. The גמרא learns from the משנה's wording that a pit and its bank combine to make ten, supporting רבי יוחנן, and starts a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The clasps looked like stars
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the previous ברייתא describes how the golden קרסים in the loops shone like stars in the sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the clasps in the loops looked like stars in the sky.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a beautiful description of the משכן. The golden clasps that joined the curtains sparkled like stars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line continues the ברייתא on the previous amud, which described the curtains of the משכן. It adds no new law. It paints a picture of how glorious the משכן looked from inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Clasps (hooks) that joined the curtains together
Loops sewn on the edges of the curtains

phrases.english: And the clasps in the loops looked
like stars in the sky.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא, begun on the previous amud, about the curtains of the משכן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The golden clasps in the loops shone like stars in the sky.

steps.title: What the lower and upper curtains were made of
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the materials: the lower curtains were of fine colored wool and linen, and the upper ones were of goat hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our Rabbis taught: The lower curtains were made of sky-blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and fine linen. The upper curtains were made of goat hair.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא tells us what each layer of the משכן's curtains was made of. This sets up the next line, which makes a surprising point about the goat-hair layer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lower curtains used expensive, beautiful materials, while the upper ones used plain goat hair. A reader would expect the fancy materials to need more skill. The ברייתא is about to say the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: Our Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:
The lower curtains were of sky-blue wool
and of purple wool and of scarlet wool
and of fine linen,
and the upper ones were of goat-hair work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues describing the משכן, now comparing the two layers of curtains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lower curtains were of fine wool and linen; upper curtains were of goat hair.

steps.title: The goat-hair curtains needed more wisdom
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא claims the upper goat-hair curtains required greater חכמה, and proves it from the different wording of the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wisdom mentioned for the upper curtains is greater than the wisdom mentioned for the lower ones. For the lower curtains it says: 'And every wise-hearted woman spun with her hands.' But for the upper curtains it says: 'And all the women whose hearts lifted them up in wisdom spun the goats.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא makes a surprising claim: the plain goat-hair curtains took more skill than the fancy ones. It proves this from the language of two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the lower curtains the תורה simply says 'wise-hearted.' For the goat hair it says the women's 'hearts lifted them up in wisdom,' which describes a higher level of skill. So the less valuable material needed the more impressive craftsmanship.

keyTerms.meaning: Their hearts lifted them up (inspired them)

phrases.english: And greater is the wisdom stated regarding the upper ones
than what was stated regarding the lower ones,
for regarding the lower ones it is written:
'And every wise-hearted woman
spun with her hands,'
while regarding the upper ones it is written:
'And all the women whose hearts lifted them up
in wisdom spun the goats.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the list of materials by claiming the goat-hair layer needed more skill.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the goat-hair curtains required greater wisdom than the fine lower curtains.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות ל״ה:כ״ה-כ״ו: 'wise-hearted' for the lower curtains versus 'whose hearts lifted them up in wisdom' for the goat hair.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: spun straight from the goats
steps.stepSummary: A teaching of רבי נחמיה explains what the extra skill was: the hair was washed and even spun while still on the live goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in the name of רבי נחמיה: The hair was washed on the goats and spun from the goats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, from רבי נחמיה, that shows exactly what the special skill was. The women washed and spun the hair while it was still attached to the goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the פסוק says 'spun the goats' and not 'spun the goat hair.' Spinning thread from a living animal is extremely hard. That is the higher חכמה the previous step pointed to.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: And it was taught in the name of Rabbi Nechemya:
It was washed on the goats
and spun from the goats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and explains the greater wisdom described in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That spinning the goat hair required unusual skill.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Teaching of רבי נחמיה: the hair was washed and spun while still on the goats.
steps.whatToRemember: The plain goat-hair curtains needed more skill than the fancy ones, because the women spun the hair straight off the living goats.

steps.title: Under, between, and beside the wagons was public domain
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה of the two balconies, רב quoting רבי חייא says the areas under, between, and beside the wagons of the משכן counted as רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Two balconies, etc.' רב said in the name of רבי חייא: With the wagons, the area under them, between them, and beside them was public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about two balconies and starts explaining it. רב teaches that the spaces around the משכן's wagons were treated as רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of carrying on שבת are learned from the work done in the משכן. The קרשים were handed between wagons through spaces that counted as public domain. That is the model the משנה about balconies with public domain below them is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: Wagons (that carried the parts of the משכן)
Etc. (the rest of the quote from the משנה)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the שבת laws in the משנה are rooted in how the משכן's wagons were set up, so the wagons' measurements matter for הלכה.

phrases.english: 'Two balconies, etc.'
Rav said in the name of Rabbi Chiya:
Wagons: beneath them and between them
and beside them is public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי גְזוּזְטְרָאוֹת כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah and returns to explaining the משנה of the two balconies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The areas beneath, between, and beside the משכן's wagons had the status of רשות הרבים.

steps.title: אביי: the gap between wagons was one wagon-length
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the space between two wagons equaled a wagon's length, which was five אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The space between one wagon and the next was the full length of a wagon. And how long was a wagon? Five אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a measurement: the gap between wagons was as long as a wagon, five אמות. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us how big the public-domain space between the wagons was. The גמרא is about to ask why the wagon had to be five אמות long.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Between one wagon and another wagon
was the full length of a wagon.
And how much is the length of a wagon?
Five cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the size of the 'between them' area mentioned by רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gap between wagons equaled a wagon's length, five אמות.

steps.title: Why five? Four and a half would be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the stacks of קרשים only needed four and a half אמות, so why was the wagon five?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need five? Four and a half would be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the wagon was five אמות long when four and a half would have held the קרשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each קרש was one and a half אמות wide, so three stacks side by side take up exactly four and a half אמות. The extra half אמה seems to have no purpose.

phrases.english: Why do I need it?
Four and a half would suffice!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the five-אמה length that אביי gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's statement that a wagon was five אמות long.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stacks of קרשים take up only four and a half אמות, so the extra half אמה looks unnecessary.

steps.title: So the קרשים would not be squeezed
steps.stepSummary: The extra space kept the קרשים from being pressed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that the beams should not be pressed together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra half אמה left room so the קרשים would not be crammed against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four and a half אמות fits the קרשים only if they are packed tightly. The extra space protected them from rubbing and damage, so the five-אמה length stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The wooden beams of the משכן

phrases.english: So that the beams should not be pressed together.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reason for the extra measurement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wagon only needed to be as long as the stacks of קרשים, four and a half אמות.
steps.terutzMaskana: An extra half אמה was needed so the קרשים would not be squeezed together.

steps.title: רבא: the sides equaled a wagon's width
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the area beside each wagon equaled the wagon's width, which was two and a half אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The sides of a wagon were the full width of a wagon. And how wide was a wagon? Two and a half אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא measures the 'beside them' area from רב's statement. It was as wide as the wagon itself, two and a half אמות. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי measured the space between wagons, and רבא now measures the space at their sides. The גמרא will again ask why the wagon had to be this size.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The sides of a wagon are the full width of a wagon.
And how much is the width of a wagon?
Two and a half cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: צִידֵּי עֲגָלָה כִּמְלֹא רֹחַב עֲגָלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to אביי's measurement, now for the 'beside them' area.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The area beside a wagon equaled the wagon's width, two and a half אמות.

steps.title: Why so wide? One and a half would be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a קרש is one and a half אמות wide, so why did the wagon need to be two and a half?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need that? One and a half אמות would be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the wagon was two and a half אמות wide when one and a half would hold a קרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors the earlier challenge. A one-and-a-half-אמה surface fits the width of a קרש, so the extra אמה seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: Why do I need it?
A cubit and a half would suffice!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the two-and-a-half-אמה width that רבא gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that a wagon was two and a half אמות wide.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A one-and-a-half-אמה surface fits a קרש, so the extra width looks unnecessary.

steps.title: So the קרשים would not wobble
steps.stepSummary: The extra width kept the long קרשים steady so they would not tip or sway.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that the beams should not wobble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wider wagon kept the ten-אמה-long קרשים stable so they would not sway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ten-אמה beam resting on a narrow one-and-a-half-אמה base would teeter. The wider wagon gave a steady base, so the two-and-a-half-אמה width stands.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer looks like step 8, but the problem is different. In step 8 the danger was the קרשים being squeezed together. Here the danger is the קרשים tipping because the base is too narrow.
steps.whatToRemember: The wagons were five אמות long and two and a half wide. In each case the extra room had a purpose: it kept the קרשים from being squeezed, and it kept them from wobbling.

phrases.english: So that the beams should not wobble.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reason for the extra measurement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wagon only needed to be as wide as a קרש, one and a half אמות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Extra width was needed so the long קרשים would rest steadily and not wobble.

steps.title: Why is a public road sixteen if the wagon area was only fifteen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: we learn that a public road is sixteen אמות wide from the משכן, but the wagon area adds up to only fifteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we hold that a road in a רשות הרבים is sixteen אמות wide, and we learn this from the משכן. The משכן's area was only fifteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds up all the measurements from the previous steps and finds a problem. They total fifteen אמות, not the sixteen we need for a public road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each wagon was two and a half אמות wide, so two wagons make five. The space between them was five. The space on each outer side was two and a half, which makes five more. That totals fifteen, yet our rule for a רשות הרבים road is sixteen, so the source and the rule do not match.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / it is established for us
A road in the public domain

phrases.english: But that which we hold

phrases.aramaic: דֶּרֶךְ רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה
phrases.english: a road of the public domain is sixteen cubits wide
phrases.notes: This is the standard minimum width of a true public road for the laws of שבת.

phrases.english: we, who learn it from the Tabernacle,
but the Tabernacle was only fifteen!
phrases.notes: 2.5 + 2.5 (the wagons) + 5 (the gap between them) + 2.5 + 2.5 (the outer sides) = 15.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds up the measurements given by אביי (step 6) and רבא (step 9), as defended in steps 8 and 11. They total only fifteen אמות, which conflicts with the sixteen-אמה rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a רשות הרבים road is sixteen אמות, since it is derived from the משכן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משכן measurements total fifteen, so they cannot be the source for sixteen.

steps.title: An extra אמה where a לוי stood
steps.stepSummary: There was one more אמה where a בן לוי stood to catch any boards that slipped. This brings the total to sixteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an extra אמה where a בן לוי would stand, so that when the boards slipped, he would catch them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adding one more אמה to the count. This was a space where a לוי stood beside the wagons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fifteen אמות counted only the wagons and the spaces around them. There was also room for a לוי to stand and catch any קרשים that slid off. Adding that one אמה gives sixteen, so the road rule fits its source.

keyTerms.meaning: A Levite, someone from the tribe of לוי

steps.whatToRemember: A רשות הרבים road is sixteen אמות wide. The number comes from the wagon area of the משכן (fifteen) plus one אמה where a לוי stood to catch slipping קרשים.

phrases.english: There was an extra cubit
where a Levite would stand
so that when the boards slipped
he would catch them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 and closes the discussion of the משכן wagons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a missing piece to the measurement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the wagons and the spaces around them counted, which makes fifteen.
steps.terutzMaskana: There was also one אמה where a לוי stood, which makes sixteen.

steps.title: משנה: the raised bank of a pit and a rock
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the raised bank of a pit, or a rock, that is ten טפחים high and four wide counts as its own domain. Moving things between it and the public area makes one liable. If it is smaller, one is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The raised bank of a pit, and a rock, that are ten טפחים high and four wide: one who takes from them or one who places on top of them is liable. If they are less than that, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a raised spot in a public area can count as a separate private domain if it is big enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something ten טפחים high and four by four טפחים wide has the status of a רשות היחיד, even when it stands in the middle of a רשות הרבים. So moving an object between it and the public area counts as carrying from one domain to another, and one is חייב. If it is shorter or narrower, it is just part of the public area, and one is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: The raised rim or bank built around a pit

steps.confusionAlert: The units change here. The wagon discussion used אמות (cubits), but this משנה's 'ten' and 'four' are טפחים (handbreadths), which are much smaller.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question: why does the משנה mention the bank of the pit and not just the pit itself?

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
The bank of a pit and the rock
that are ten handbreadths high
and four handbreadths wide

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹטֵל מֵהֶן וְהַנּוֹתֵן עַל גַּבָּן — חַיָּיב
phrases.english: one who takes from them, or one who places on top of them, is liable
less than that, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the משכן discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bank or rock that is ten טפחים high and four wide is a separate domain. Moving objects between it and the public area makes one liable. If it is smaller, one is exempt.

steps.title: Why mention the bank and not just the pit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה says 'the bank of a pit' when it could have simply said 'a pit.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why does the משנה need to say 'the bank of a pit and the rock'? Let it say 'the pit and the rock'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the משנה's wording. It asks why the extra word 'bank' was added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain pit ten טפחים deep would already teach the rule for depth, and the rock would teach the rule for height. So naming the bank seems unnecessary. The גמרא assumes the extra word must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
Why do I need it? (asks why something is there)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Why do I need it to teach
'the bank of a pit and the rock'?
Let it teach 'the pit and the rock'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the exact wording of the משנה in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra word 'bank' (חוליית) in the משנה teaches

steps.title: The wording supports רבי יוחנן: the pit and its bank combine
steps.stepSummary: The word 'bank' supports רבי יוחנן, who says that the depth of a pit and the height of its bank add together to make ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יוחנן, for רבי יוחנן said: a pit and its bank combine to make ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה said 'bank' on purpose. It is teaching the same idea that רבי יוחנן taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pit does not need to be ten טפחים deep by itself, and the bank does not need to be ten טפחים high by itself. If the pit's depth plus the bank's height together reach ten, the whole thing counts as a רשות היחיד. The משנה's wording backs up this rule of רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, a pit's depth and its bank's height add up together toward the ten טפחים needed for a רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yochanan
for Rabbi Yochanan said:
A pit and its bank combine to make ten.
phrases.notes: For example, a pit that is 6 טפחים deep with a bank that is 4 טפחים high totals 10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by explaining what the word 'bank' teaches.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Bank' teaches that the pit's depth and the bank's height combine toward ten טפחים, which supports רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a pit in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that also supports רבי יוחנן. It starts with a pit in a רשות הרבים that is ten deep and four wide, from which one may not draw water on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: a pit in a רשות הרבים that is ten deep and four wide, one may not draw water from it on שבת...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a ברייתא as more support for רבי יוחנן. This is only the opening of the ברייתא; the part that actually proves the point continues right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit that is ten טפחים deep and four wide is a רשות היחיד, so lifting water out of it into the public area is forbidden on שבת. This opening line sets up the basic case. The ברייתא's next words, on the next amud, will show that the bank can count toward the ten.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)
A private domain for the laws of שבת

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
A pit in the public domain
that is ten handbreadths deep and four wide
one may not draw water from it on Shabbat
phrases.notes: The pit is a private domain, so bringing water up into the public domain is carrying between domains. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's rule from step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that a pit and its bank combine to make ten טפחים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about drawing water from a pit in a רשות הרבים on שבת (it continues on the next amud)
